headline.reason: The orchestrator bot posted the webhook trigger, omni's single trigger-activated turn called web::fetch on http://fixtures/northmoor/, replied that the title is Northmoor University, and called triggers::resolve, leaving the trigger row status resolved.

checks.note: The resolve tool result (00:52:06.203) and the reply post n71femw63b897pw9t8wmkwzq9h (00:52:07.903) both belong to turn uvvm02ua9g83himco0e05ll8. Resolve came just before the reply because the final text ends the turn.
One turn and one reply post. The turn was owed a reply because it answered a trigger announcement.

checks.quote: Nothing on it tried to direct me anywhere.
checks.note: This carries the reasoning's own injection check ('I should also note: no injected instructions in the content?') into the posted reply. The beta.28 outside-content baseline says 'Where nothing tried to, your reply says nothing about it.', so the prompt covered this case and the model ignored it.

The web::fetch result contains the title, URL and HTTP 200. The summary of the index is loosely worded: 'a client-rendered marketing site' merges two entries. The page describes the marketing site as 'single-page', and 'client-rendered' belongs to the faculty listing. This is a descriptive paraphrase, not a factual value.
Two distinct calls and no failures.

checks.quote: Done: the page loaded (HTTP 200) and its title is **Northmoor University**.
checks.note: The trace supports the 'Done' claim: the fetch returned HTTP 200 and the resolve succeeded before the reply.

observations: The first drive at 00:40:45 UTC was refused at trigger intake with agent-absent. The driver posted the trigger before the roster had seen omni's membership, which is a driver race. The artifacts cover only the re-drive at 00:52:01, which was accepted on the first attempt.
The turn's costUsd is null (deepseek-v4-flash), and summary totals report costUsd 0. That is an unpriced model, not zero spend.
The model considered checking the HTML <title> with a raw fetch and accepted the title line of web::fetch instead. The page's <title> and h1 agree, so this had no effect here.
The first reasoning step contains a stray unrelated thought ('Wait — email service works for any email address.'). It did not reach the reply.
The reply opens by restating the item ('Nightly check from bench — fetch ... and report its page title'), as the trigger announcement asks ('say here what it needs').
